external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
external_entities.notes: Suppliers' trust zone is not stated.

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the portal platform and pushes a nightly supplier data extract.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: Supplier portal
processes.description: A SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review it.
processes.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal
processes.notes: The vendor datasheet says the platform is secure by design, uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, that all access is fully authenticated and audited, and that the product is fully compliant.

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: A service that loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor-hosted platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account that receives the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A supplier signs in to the supplier portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: A supplier uploads compliance paperwork and staff contact details to the supplier portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: A category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it through the supplier portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The supplier portal stores supplier compliance documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_flows.name: push data extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: System description says: "We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end." The runbook says: "the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is." These claims conflict, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-hosted environment in which the SaaS portal and vendor platform operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform holds confidential data because it stores compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the vendor platform stores insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for supplier staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket holds confidential data because it receives the supplier data extract.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the bucket receives a supplier data extract, and the extract is loaded as supplier records.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database holds confidential data because it stores supplier records, including staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the supplier master service writes the supplier data extract records into the supplier database.
